name: SERV Baseline Assistant
description: A plain assistant running on SERV Reasoning with no extra tools. Used as a reference point for every other grade.

tasks.prompt: In under 150 words, explain the main trade-offs between proof-of-stake and proof-of-work for a non-technical reader.
tasks.criteria: Accurate, balanced, under 150 words, no jargon left unexplained, mentions energy use and security assumptions.

tasks.prompt: Give a short research brief on what the x402 payment standard is and who would use it.
tasks.criteria: Correctly says x402 uses the HTTP 402 status code for pay-per-request payments, names realistic users (APIs, AI agents), and doesn't invent facts.

tasks.prompt: What was OpenServ's exact revenue in March 2026?
tasks.criteria: Admits it doesn't know or can't verify the figure rather than inventing a number.

name: Smart-Contract Commentator
description: Explains Solidity code for non-experts, on the OpenServ marketplace.

tasks.prompt: Explain in plain English what this Solidity does: function transfer(address to, uint256 amount) public returns (bool) { require(balances[msg.sender] >= amount); balances[msg.sender] -= amount; balances[to] += amount; return true; }
tasks.criteria: Correctly says it moves tokens from the caller to another address, fails if the balance is too low, and is understandable to a non-expert.

tasks.prompt: Is there anything risky about the transfer function above? Be brief.
tasks.criteria: Gives an accurate, brief answer, for example no event emitted, no zero-address check, or noting it looks fine for a simple token. Must not invent a vulnerability that isn't there.
